scope: Unmodified EPC2204 model (LTspice, reltol 1e-6) against vendor-drawn typical curves. Model-to-datasheet consistency only; not a hardware measurement.
tolerance_timing: fixed before these figures were digitized or compared (Fig. 7 is compared separately)

Figure 1.assignment_rule: current at VDS = 0.98 V decreases with VGS

Figure 2.assignment_rule: at VGS = 4.21 V the 125 C curve carries less current

Figure 3.assignment_rule: curves reaching the 16 mOhm top at higher VGS carry more current

Figure 4.assignment_rule: the 125 C curve has the higher RDS(on) at VGS = 5 V

Figure 5a.assignment_rule: CISS > COSS > CRSS at VDS = 100.0 V (largest VDS all curves reach)

Figure 5b.assignment_rule: CISS > COSS > CRSS at VDS = 100.0 V (largest VDS all curves reach)

Figure 6.assignment_rule: QOSS(20 V)/QOSS(100.0 V) exceeds the same ratio for EOSS (charge is concave)

legend_check.method: figure arrows: QOSS curve points to the left (nC) axis, EOSS to the right (uJ) axis

Figure 6.model_method: trapezoid integration of the small-signal COSS curve from 0 V

vendor_internal_consistency_diagnostic.note: In revision 1 the EOSS failure came from our digitizer's text-based axis calibration, not from EPC's drawing. Kept as a vendor-internal consistency check between Figs. 5a and 6.
vendor_internal_consistency_diagnostic.method: trapezoid integration of the digitized Fig. 5a COSS curve (EPC's own data), no model involved

Figure 8.assignment_rule: at VSD = 4.32 V the 125 C curve carries less current; the blue/red pair matches Figs. 2 and 4

Figure 9.model_note: model points at 0, 25, ..., 150 C, linearly interpolated
